timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, I am Luga Skon and I am in Long Beach Comic Con 2014 with Mr. Jim Cummings.
Hello, thanks for inviting me out to play.
So what do you do?
Well, I am a voice actor and I do voices for a lot of cartoon characters and sing and say things like, in a world.
Stuff like that.
So what do you give us another example of that?
Well, I suppose I could do some Winnie the Poe for you but I don't have any honey.
But I can't do any bouncing because I left my stripes at home.
So how big is creativity to you?
Well, I think creativity is everything to everybody.
I think because without creation, we wouldn't be here. But you knew that.
But I think the thing is you just can't be afraid. You can't be timid.
And don't be afraid to make mistakes and jump out there and I had a friend of mine, Alan Koss, an actor.
He said that when you're doing animated voices and things like that, it's so broad and it's so this and that.
But it's the freedom to be a jerk or an A-hole is actually what he said but I won't say that here.
So if you do it enough and do it right, it seems to work out.
I guess so. You know, it helps to be a little fearless, I think.
So what would you want to tell students and our audience who are kind of afraid to show their creative side?
Well, you know, I can tell you as far as being a voice actor goes.
The way I used to do it, I was always in plays as a kid because people said, well, how do you start?
How do you get into it?
I was always in plays and I'll be 10 years old and instead of wanting to be the little prince,
I wanted to be the monster or the ogre or the wizard because it was, you know, a little more, something that sink your teeth into.
And it was always in those plays as a kid and in musicals and I used to do impressions of my relatives who were not famous but they were good impressions.
So that was like a new character.
And if you do an impression of somebody that everybody knows, very famous and it doesn't sound like them at all, that's a new character too.
So, you know, you can just put them in your little mental roller decks and go back and pull them out when you need it.
That's how I did it and I didn't know that it was supposed to be tough to break into so I just blundered in.
So that's one good way to do it.
They say, go hunting with a shotgun.
So they weren't waiting on me when I showed up so jump in and do it.
Everything is honey, everywhere I see, everything is honey and that's quite alright with me.
Oh, it's a dangerous pass I bounce but I bounce it alone because the hunter decarwood needs a hero poop hair and I'm the only one.
So on what are your current projects right now?
Well, let's see, there's Goldie and Little Bear which is a continuation of the Little Red Riding Hood story.
I play the Big Bad Wolf.
I play Bad Guys 2.
It's okay.
And Nomeo and Juliet too.
I think the working title is Sherlock Nomes.
We're going to be starting on that in January.
Elton John and David for Anishis Partners that was their movie for Disney.
A new movie coming out with John Cleese and a bunch of other people animated called Animal Crackers.
And another one that they don't have the title for yet so I can't tell you.
I guess Star Wars Rebels is going to be coming to a TV near you.
So I'm sure I'm forgetting a few but you'll just have to stay tuned.
We'll definitely check it out.
Well, thank you for giving us a time to tell us your insight about creativity.
Well, thanks Lou. Thanks for coming out and hanging out.
Thank you.
And stay just as potsy as you can.
2TFN.

youtube_description:
Voice actor Jim Cummings answers the question "Why is Creativity Important?" at Long Beach Comic Con. A voice actor and singer, Jim has appeared in almost 400 roles. He is known for voicing Darkwing Duck, Dr. Robotnik from Sonic the Hedgehog, and Pete, as well as being the current voice of both Winnie the Pooh and Tigger, as well as the Tasmanian Devil. He has performed in numerous animated Disney and DreamWorks movies including Aladdin, The Lion King, Antz, The Road to El Dorado, Shrek, and The Princess and the Frog. 

Voices of Creativity is a student produced series where we ask professionals from all industries the question "Why is Creativity Important?" and learn how it influences their careers.
